relevance_note: Case report of a family with a LAMP2 variant: "The LAMP2 c.741+2T>C mutation was identified in the proband (hemizygous) and his mother (heterozygous)".
method_note: Hand extraction, no tables in the paper; JSON assembled by a short script from hand-chosen values. Two in-scope people: the proband (label 'patient', rule 5; the paper uses only role words) and his mother. Other relatives ('the rest relatives', including the father whose DNA was used as minigene template) are described only as a group tested negative / without anomalies, with no individual-level fact, so they get no rows. Ages 19 (proband, at referral) and 42 (mother) are ages at presentation; a 2-year follow-up followed, so age at last evaluation is left not reported; no age at onset or diagnosis stated (proband had a '3-month history'). Normal 'liver function' recorded as excluded 'abnormal liver function' but the checklist item 'elevated liver enzymes (transaminases)' left not reported because transaminases are not named. Mother's normal echocardiography ('did not show obvious anomalies') is a whole-investigation finding and is not used to exclude LVH or other specific cardiac items (D-27). Intraventricular block is not mapped to atrioventricular block. 'No family history of sudden cardiac death' is family-level and not recorded. LVEF 50% is recorded as detail only; the paper does not call it reduced. Group exclusions use the named groups 'all the family members' and 'the two patients in the pedigree'. Variant type, functional evidence and pathogenicity for the mother come from sentences naming this exact variant / the family. No contradictions found.
